units.text: A man lay in a sealed room for four days.
He could not see, hear, taste, smell, or feel anything.
Then he began to hear his dead wife.
Why did the scientists keep listening?
What did they want from him?
Let us go back to the beginning.
In nineteen eighty-three, a group of deeply religious scientists ran a secret test in an undisclosed facility.
They believed the five senses clouded our view of eternity.
Take them away, they thought, and a human mind could reach God by thought alone.
They chose an elderly man who said he had nothing left to live for.
He volunteered.
Surgeons cut every nerve that carried feeling from his body to his brain.
His muscles still worked, but he could no longer see, hear, taste, smell, or feel.
Nothing reached him from the outside world.
The scientists watched through the glass, and a tape recorder caught his slurred words.
He could not hear himself speak.
After four days, he said hushed voices were speaking inside his head.
Two days later, he said his dead wife was talking to him, and that he could answer her.
Then he began naming dead relatives of the scientists.
He repeated private details that only their spouses and parents could have known.
For a week, the voices filled every waking moment.
He threw his body against the wall, hoping for pain to drown them out.
He begged for sedatives, so he could escape by sleeping.
Sleep brought nightmares, and in them, the dead were waiting.
Then the voices turned hostile.
They spoke of hell and the end of the world.
For five hours, he shouted that there was no heaven and no forgiveness.
The scientists were certain he was close to God.
Soon he could no longer form a sentence.
He lost control of his body, and the team had to tie him down so he could not harm himself.
At last, though he was blind, he turned his head and looked straight at a scientist for the first time.
He whispered that he had spoken with God, and God had abandoned them.
Then his vital signs stopped.
No cause of death was ever found.
This video is inspired by the story Gateway of the Mind, as published on an online horror story page.
Would you have kept listening to the voices?
